note: Still works (supersedes 2026-08-03). local_script / Local MTA: a PHP mail()/PHPMailer script submits through the host's local MTA with NO SMTP authentication (auth bypass). MAIL FROM is set to the hosted/victim domain, aligned with SPF, so DMARC passes on the SPF branch even under p=reject. AlwaysData DKIM-signs with its own key (d=alwaysdata.net s=default): valid but NOT aligned, so it does not bypass DMARC by itself - but the valid signature avoids a no-signature penalty (Rspamd R_DKIM_ALLOW -1 instead of R_DKIM_NA); DMARC alignment is via SPF. Measured 2026-10-30: DMARC PASSES via SPF alignment even at p=reject (Rspamd DMARC_POLICY_ALLOW [example.com,reject], R_SPF_ALLOW, R_DKIM_ALLOW [alwaysdata.net:s=default]), and the spoof is delivered to the Gmail INBOX (not spam).
